name: Check an object’s accession number and provenance

uses.action: Connect the two catalogued pots to their recorded places in the excavation and keep the empty space visible.
Separate the earlier surface from the later label before lighting both for the visitor.

name: Anchor a claim to the date of its source

uses.action: Compare the dated workshop receipt with later advice and decide which stage of development the other workshop may compare.

name: Cross-check a family account of an object

uses.action: Set the signed account alongside a neighbour’s memory and show which witness is still missing.
Trace the handled object along its later journey and consult a local account before giving it a place.

name: Keep conflicting expert evidence in view

uses.action: Set two interviews from different visits alongside their actual questions before carrying the disputed account onward.

name: Show two readings of the same evidence

uses.action: Move the label and light the surface so the visitor can distinguish an observation from the curator’s reading.
Keep the documented ledger entry visible while arranging clearly possible scenes around its gap.

name: Ask who can make a truth claim public

uses.action: Follow the drummer’s route, then see whose actions the official petition’s verbs permit the reader to recognize.

name: Balance certainty against the cost of acting

uses.action: Seal a prediction or mark a result that should halt the work before passing the decision to the watcher.

name: Examine how local conventions shape an objective measure

uses.action: Keep the grower’s identification alongside the catalogue name and test which distinctions survive a folding tag.

name: Identify values behind standards of justification

uses.action: Decide what justifies a place on the last ferry when order of arrival conflicts with a promise.

name: Compare explanatory strength with confidence

uses.action: Take a proposed account of the galaxy’s rotation to a second galaxy or seal a fresh prediction.

name: Test a truth claim from a second standpoint

uses.action: Set the two window views against a thread reference and let the next viewer recover their positions.

name: Trace who can set the terms of an interpretation

uses.action: Follow a missing source back to the intake desk and decide how the request it failed to answer stays visible.

name: Ask what counts as evidence in this community

uses.action: Seek the builder’s permission for a trace of the grip and compare what can be seen from paddling height.

name: Identify a value choice in an objective measure

uses.action: Swap gain and loss notices over queues with the same passenger count and watch their reception.

name: Consider who must answer for an explanation

uses.action: Lay a kitchen plan beneath the road or follow the resident and traveller separately so the time estimate has named consequences.

name: Give reasons for an interpretation

uses.action: Set the vessel pattern beside clay and settlement evidence before choosing how to present a possible reading.

name: Revisit confidence from someone else’s position

uses.action: Move between the family’s chair and the servants’ door before deciding how confidently the witness can describe the hall.

name: Follow the power to retain or exclude evidence

uses.action: Compare bill, signature book and index to see whose labour is retrievable by a later visitor.

name: Distinguish truth from a persuasive explanation

uses.action: Test the competing bell and cloud stories against a dry trial before carrying the causal account onward.

name: Trace responsibilities attached to cultural knowledge

uses.action: Put hosts in charge of the return key or arrange the findings’ return before setting an account loose.

name: Expose the grounds for a claim to objectivity

uses.action: Align the raw traces and the mirror reference so another observer can check the comparison.

name: Connect authority with accountability to affected people

uses.action: Hand over the first question or secure a return visit so a host can change what the investigator has authority to do.
After hearing two sources, give the families or the dawn shift a concrete way of calling the council back.

name: Compare the values behind two interpretations

uses.action: Frame the individual seed against the workshop and decide what attention the makers receive in the account.

name: Trace three interacting concepts in one case

uses.action: Compare the ledger, loose slip and visible gap to decide how evidence, interpretation and responsibility constrain the story.

name: Trace a reported saying through its named transmitters

uses.action: Trace a report back narrator by narrator or bring an excluded reader to its context before choosing the account to carry.
Lay names along both transmission routes and retain the attributions attached to their different endings.

name: Investigate a particular thing in a Neo-Confucian account

uses.action: Roll the worn rim and compare that result with the water line and the marked unit in Zhu Xi’s workshop.

name: Examine how a Kerala mathematician reasoned about a series

uses.action: Assemble a finite part of the circle and carry forward either the remaining gap or the rule for continuing the construction.

name: Keep people and limits visible when interpreting a tradition

uses.action: Ask what is public and leave the authority for further explanation with the custodian.
Use a permitted practice strip or a public technique and leave the closed drawer with its maker.

name: Compare missed warnings with false alarms

uses.action: Move the clip across recorded nights and weigh households woken in dry weather against steps flooded without a call.

name: Separate measurable risk from uncertainty with unknown odds

uses.action: Move a rule drawn from a familiar shoal into an unknown inlet and decide how far it can travel with the lookout.

name: Revisit a provisional scientific claim as evidence arrives

uses.action: Keep the observed graph, the reviewer’s question and the possible future use distinct in what the next reader receives.
Reopen the chalked bridge times after Joss times the hinged plank in both directions, rerun the lane and republish.

name: Compare plans across several plausible futures

uses.action: Change an assumption on yesterday’s road plan or lay its cost alongside the historical route.
Compare the same lane in clear air and fog, and try moving the single runner before posting the first knock.

name: Vary a parameter and track the model’s response

uses.action: Vary the single alarm threshold in a replay of the same six nights and examine the changed outcomes.
Hold the lane fixed and change the shutter; then change the runner’s first stop while the tower remains hidden.

name: Distinguish an estimate from its range of uncertainty

uses.action: Rebuild the calculation or mark the landing band so another person can see what a single reported number hides.

name: Recalculate a rate when the counted population changes

uses.action: Change the counting group from four respondents to six households and act on the difference between 4/4 and 4/6.

name: Measure how far a proxy stands from its target

uses.action: Compare the tally used to reward a keeper with the arrivals it is meant to record.
Count loan transactions, compare the requests the counter misses and keep the waiting group’s need visible when placing the rests.

name: Distinguish expertise from the power to compel

uses.action: Compare the signed version with the bare argument and the objection before choosing which reading the clerk sees.

name: Distinguish methodological doubt from anxiety

uses.action: Mark an observation that would stop a forecast, giving doubt a test another watcher can use.

name: Compare quantitative and narrative historical reasoning

uses.action: Move the account among a single storm, a series of seasonal routes and a century ledger to compare different historical explanations.

name: Read political and social histories of the same event

uses.action: Place the reign heading beside local street work and a local calendar to see whose history the sequence records.

name: Weigh excavation or sampling against future preservation

uses.action: Use the exposed section, tray and standing strip to decide what to inspect now and what to leave for another observer.

name: Weigh museum storage against living community use

uses.action: Weigh the custody slip against a community request at the crate and choose who gets the first hearing.

name: Construct a counterclaim from within one discipline

uses.action: Make one anthropologist’s interpretation answerable to another’s evidence by comparing the questions and dates of both visits.

name: Balance assertive wording with room for uncertainty

uses.action: Place two possible scenes beside a documented gap or light the gap without filling it in.

name: Name the knower or method behind an action

uses.action: Change the petition’s verbs over the same square and see which version lets the organiser appear as an actor.

name: Surface assumptions hidden in a familiar saying

uses.action: Trace a worker’s day beyond the overseer’s count and test the assumption hidden in the notebook’s label.

name: Distinguish an imagined case from real-world evidence

uses.action: Lay the imagined change beside the actual route before choosing how the next traveller may use either.
